SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JULY 28, 2025 - 06:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 2:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 2:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. 11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, JULY 28, 2025, 6:00
PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 6:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Juno Smalley, New Life Community Church.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Extra – AYSO Region 54 Team (Boys U10).

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  An informational update regarding the ABC Unified School District.

  An informational update regarding the ABC Unified School District was given by Ernie
  Nishii, ABC Unified School District Board President.

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

  5B.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Jaxson Janecky, Tyler Schwichow, Maduran Aravinthan, and Joshua Arriaga (Extra –
  AYSO Region 54 Team members); Mike Schwichow, Coach and Coach Administrator;
  Veronica Janecky, Regional Commissioner (AYSO 50th Anniversary).

  Pankl Aerospace Systems (Business Spotlight).

  Yash Samineni, Sarvesh Thirmualai, Mohit Banda, Vishal Sivakumar, and Alvin Kishore
  (Rank of Eagle Scout).

  5C.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions, and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

  5D.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad hoc
  working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5D.  (continued)

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the next
  City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda (scheduled for Thursday, August 14,
  2025).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Jose Badillo expressed concerns regarding parkway tree removal/reforestation in the
  neighborhood adjacent to Marquardt Avenue, Artesia Boulevard, and Carmenita
  Boulevard.

  Kirit Chauhan thanked the City for allowing Commission and Committee members to
  attend the 2025 AAPI LEAD National Summit and provided information regarding
  educational opportunities provided. He also expressed concern regarding economic
  disparities in the community.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the two (2) written comments submitted for Item 6, by
  the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for
  copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, July 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration, by Mayor Pro
  Tem Johnson.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to approve the Thursday,
  July 10, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 0 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Johnson

City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 9

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated July 28, 2025 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  July 28, 2025  $4,459,328.64 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget Amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to authorize an
  administrative-initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 budget amendment in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2025-19/CSA No. 2025-02 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  Account/Project: Multiple
  Amount: $852,900
  Justification: A carryover of unexpended funds from the prior fiscal year is requested
  for capital equipment that was ordered but not received by fiscal year-end, due to
  ongoing nationwide supply chain delays. Carrying over these funds will ensure that the
  necessary appropriations remain available to complete the purchases once the equipment
  is delivered (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY

  exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Alvin Papa, Director of Public Works/City Engineer.

  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of proposed water rate adjustment options to support long-
  term fiscal sustainability (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Alvin Papa, Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Kirit Chauhan requested the City provide more information to residents regarding water
  rate adjustments; expressed concern regarding drastic adjustments to water rates; and
  commented regarding a need to rescind City regulations related to irrigation.

  Charlie Joslin expressed concerns regarding water rate adjustments, supporting further
  subsidies from the City’s General Fund.

  Catherine Pascual expressed support for infrastructure improvements and a combination
  of the potential rate adjustment scenarios provided in the agenda report associated with
  this item. She also requested the City issue water bills on a monthly cycle.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the three (3) written comments submitted for Item 9A, by
  the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for
  copies of the written comment submitted for this meeting can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to conduct research regarding the
  staff time and resources required to issue water bills on a monthly cycle.

(minutes continue on the next page)

  1. Approve progression of the water rate adjustment process in accordance with
  Scenario 2b, as presented in the agenda report associated with this item,
  incorporating critical infrastructure investment with General Fund support, phased out
  over time, including updated meter charges based on meter capacity and elimination
  of base minimum units, as follows:

  Five-Year Capital Improvement Project  General Fund Support
  Critical Projects Only ($23 million)  Gradual phased out over five
  (5) years

  Revenue  February  January  January  January  January
  Adjustments  2026  2027  2028  2029  2030
  Scenario 2b  50%  30%  25%  20%  5%

  and;

  2. Direct staff to finalize the water rate study report accordingly and present the final
  report for City Council review and consideration at a future meeting (COUNCIL).

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  None.
